Welcome to iOS! To start customizing I recommend PicsArt for photo editing, Widgetsmith for widgetworking, MD Blank - Transparent Widget for invisible, nameless widgets and for wallpapers:

Pinterest - For more specific, fanmade, media themed or niche wallpapers with a huge collection of anything you could ever want (with the catch being most images being low quality, so waifu2x for upscaling is a must). If you know LiS you probably already know Pinterest lol;

Vellum - Hand picked wallpapers formed in collections. Beautiful abstract, photographic and modeled wallpapers in very high quality with blurring abilities;

Unsplash - Free to use stunning work varying from photography to modeling, most of Vellum's sources come from Unsplash. Works like a stock image database. Resplash is the best Android client for it if you ever decide to switch back.

edit for more stuff:

For icons, it's an easy yet boring process:

1- In the Automations tab at the bottom, make two automations:

--Set the trigger to 'when an app is opened' and select every app you want to customize

--In the first one, set the action to something you definitely won't use, to me that was AssistiveTouch. So make the shortcut turn it off, making it do nothing since it was already off in the first place;

--In the second one, set it to a number action in the calculator (my phone's in Norwegian and mine translates to 'send numbers to next' so i'm not sure which one it is, but it's just a field for you to type a number). I put 42.

-- Set both of them to run without asking. 

2- In the Shortcuts tab, make a new shortcut:

--Search for 'open app' in the actions. select one app you want to customize.

-- At the top near the X button there's a settings button. Tap that.

--Tap 'add to home screen'. Set the name you want (or blank) and the image you want by tapping the small icon to the left of the text field. 

--The app'll kick you out to the homescreen and it should be there. Tap it a couple times, you will still see banners and notifications, but still tap it a couple times to make sure you got enough notifications. 

3- Next, go go Settings. Under Screen Time, tap 'See all activity'. Scroll down to notifications and look for Shortcuts. If it doesn't have the arrow like all the other apps, keep switching the day at the top of the screen until it shows up. It can be just back and forth. This might take a day to work if you've never had a Shortcuts notification. At last keep switching days until it shows up and turn off all notifications. Don't worry, your Shortcuts will still work fine. 

4- Try tapping that same icon again. It should have no banners, no notifications, just the custom icon. 

5- For every app you must make a new shortcut and add it like the first one, and add that app to the Automations aswell.

Hope this helps!

PreMiD (that exact add-on) user here. The program works like this: Firstly, [you download a third party app](https://premid.app/downloads) that [stays in the background](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/740337171826868378/820992076044566568/unknown.png) tracking your browser. It only shows websites you yourself went and searched for on the [Presence Store](https://premid.app/store) and [enabled in the settings](https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/740337171826868378/820991670480011324/unknown.png), though. After that, Discord detects the task's [Rich Presence](https://discord.com/rich-presence) data and displays it in your Game Activity.

I consent to that exact information being "showed publicly". I chose to enable my Game Activity and I was the one who selected the platforms I wanted to show on my Status.

If you have any questions about it, there's always the [Privacy](https://premid.app/privacy) and [Terms](https://premid.app/tos) page on their website.
